bluf: Adswerve is a Denver based data, media and technology consultancy selling Google and Adobe stack expertise to enterprise brands and other agencies; it calls itself the #1 Google Marketing Partner in the US with 950+ clients. It is pushing MiaProva, its Adobe Target management platform, deeper into the Adobe and Google data stacks, and runs its own Google ads (125 in the Transparency Center, 32 in the last 30 days). The record points it toward measurement and orchestration rather than media buying. What a rival should know: all 13 clients on record are names without described work, and it sells CRO while its own homepage shows no testing tool.
doing:
The positioning line reads as a predictive marketing consultancy applying data, analytics, media and AI for brands and agencies, specialising in Google and Adobe stacks: in plain words, a measurement and martech shop that also buys media and sells to other agencies. The headline claim of #1 Google Marketing Partner in the US with 950+ brand and agency clients is quoted as a claim; the about page adds 170+ Google Marketing Platform certifications.

The sold mix leads with Data & Measurement, score 3 and the only lead line: a Meridian MMM for Alaska Airlines and an FTD MMM that cut TV budget 30%. Four core lines score 2. AI Automation: AI Solutions is one of four service pillars, with a Six Flags GenAI case. CRO: MiaProva manages Adobe Target testing programs, and a Container Store product page case. Paid Search: Betterment CPA down 10%, airline conversions +149% for Cramer-Krasselt, Crowd Cow +108% for Ovative. Programmatic & CTV: Adswerve Premium Supply, and LinkedIn ads for premium CTV, DOOH and audio buying. Partners listed: Google Marketing Platform, Adobe Solution Partner, Snowflake SELECT Partner, Amplitude and Google's GIP data strength program.

AI posture: AI sold as a data service, AI ready data foundations, ad copy at scale, sentiment analysis and Adobe MCP tooling through MiaProva. No AI search or GEO line.

Moves in date order: in 2026-04 MiaProva added Adobe Real-Time CDP, CJA, GA4 and BigQuery integrations (dated by the sitemap); in 2026 it won Adobe's Americas Emerging Partner of the Year, a third straight year. Undated releases: Tom Zawacki appointed Chief Executive Officer, the Adswerve Premium Supply launch, and the Google GIP partnership.

The record lists no pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a company of its kind: an AI search or answer engine service (a blog URL on AEO and GEO foundations is the only trace), any owned audience or CRM line, and no news, case studies or jobs on record.
clients:
The record describes an enterprise client type serving brands and agencies, with verticals listed as Travel & airlines, Financial services, Media & publishing, Healthcare, Retail & ecommerce, Entertainment & sports, Technology and Agencies, and the home market is the US, with Denver, CO the only office listed.

The needs read holds 13 clients, all from case study pages, and codes every one N0, engagement named only: the pages name the client and the read captured nothing about the work. Alaska Airlines came for a Meridian MMM and FTD for an MMM that cut TV budget 30%, data and measurement work observed in the capability notes. Six Flags is a GenAI case, AI and automation. The Container Store is a product page optimization case, web build and platform under conversion design. Betterment is a search bidding case with CPA down 10%, paid performance. Two agency clients came for paid search execution, also paid performance: Cramer-Krasselt with airline conversions +149% and Ovative Group with Crowd Cow +108%. Cedars-Sinai, Condé Nast, Gannett, The Arena Group, World Surf League and Avid Technology are names with no described work; their need is inferred from what the agency leads with, data and measurement.

One client is shared: The Container Store also sits on pmg's book. The book is entirely names only by the read's own count, 13 of 13.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places it best for KJ9, measurement gets worse before it gets better, and KJ4, the platforms are absorbing the execution layer. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that these enterprise and publisher clients buy measurement rebuilds and platform orchestration next, and there is a roughly even chance that the agency clients, Ovative Group and Cramer-Krasselt, take the bidding work in house as platform automation absorbs it.
house: Say and do: two lines tested. Paid Search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 125 in the Transparency Center and 32 in the last 30 days. CRO is contradicted: it sells CRO and no testing tool is detected on its own homepage, its one listed gap. openings:
The contradiction to lead with is CRO: Adswerve sells it, MiaProva manages Adobe Target programs, and no testing tool is detected on its own homepage. A rival running a visible testing program on its own site very likely, moderate confidence, wins the CRO conversation at The Container Store and the Adobe Target accounts MiaProva serves. Falsifier: a testing tool appearing on adswerve.com, or a case study of its own site under test.

The two agency clients are contestable: Cramer-Krasselt and Ovative Group buy bidding execution, the hours KJ4 says the platforms absorb, and an offer priced on outputs likely undercuts a consultancy with no listed pricing model (P5 unknown).

The book is an opening: 13 of 13 clients are names only, and The Container Store already sits on pmg's book, a client that shops. It sells paid search with no test of ads inside AI assistants (P8 absent) and no AI search line (P1 absent): the first rival with audited AI visibility numbers leads with the number. Most exposed to KJ5 through Programmatic & CTV, so Adswerve Premium Supply is the line to price against, low confidence, since only a press release and LinkedIn ads stand behind it.
